liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dear Mr. Fantasy** (4 reviews): Brent sang Dear Mr. Fantasy on B3 organ; it hooked the reviewer, whose first show this was; Reviewer singles out Dear Mr. Fantasy and Hey Jude as standout moments of the night [15][16][17][21]
- ***Bird Song** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer links this show to the Without A Net release's sound for many songs; Bird Song from this show appears on the Without A Net release [2][24]
- **Turn on Your Lovelight** (1 review): Reviewer felt the band ran low on energy after Hey Jude and closed the set with Lovelight [14]
- **One More Saturday Night** (1 review): Bob sounds especially energized on this One More Saturday Night [18]
- **Hey Jude** (1 other source): Hey Jude Finale is not tracked as a separate song [3]
- Crowd was let down when Knockin' began, since many were hoping for an Attics song instead [14]
- Uploader gets chills and a grin when the Playing reprise arrives two songs later [6]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd89-12-09 01 Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd89-12-09 02 Touch Of Grey**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd89-12-09 04 Row Jimmy**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd89-12-09 05 Mexicali Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd89-12-09 06 Cumberland Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd89-12-09 07 Bird Song**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd89-12-09 08 One More Saturday Night**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]
- **gd89-12-09 09 Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]

## The recordings

- **gd1989-12-09.140198.dsbd.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): source not stated; 20 songs; 149 min [1]
- **gd1989-12-09.fob.french.76273.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 18 songs; 147 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the recording faithful to the live sound and calls it an early binaural recording [20]
- **gd1989-12-09.fob.french.35373.sbeok.flac24**: source not stated; 19 songs; 147 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd1989-12-09.sbd.miller-ladner.5450.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 147 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [6]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says Charlie Miller's work gives good sound from a huge hall, equal or better than the other soundboard [23]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended, standing on the floor about ten feet in front of the soundboard [20]
- Reviewer recalls full surround speakers at the arena top, with Drums and Space swirling around the room [24]
- Uploader had seats behind the stage, viewing the drummers and the throbbing front-row crowd [6]
- Many balloons popped throughout the show, as at most 1989 shows [6]
- Reviewer sees 1989 as among the last of the good years, though this show is not an all-time great [17]
- Reviewer thinks Row Jimmy was better in Sacramento the next year, and that this show is overshadowed by other shows [19]
- Reviewer finds the band fairly tight and this soundboard comparable to the other soundboard of the date [23]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1989-12-09.140198.dsbd.miller.clugston.flac1648**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix Master Soundbonard Dat 16/48 > Dat clone 16/48 directly from Dat master [1]. Also: Cassette source supplies the tuning and the first four seconds of Touch Of Grey [1]
- **gd1989-12-09.fob.french.76273.sbeok.flac16**: source: Sennheiser MKE2002 omni's HRTF stealth stereo -> Sony TC-D5M [2]. Also: Transferred via Tascam DVRA1000 in USB2.0 mode, then Mac G4 import, FLAC compression and 16/44 conversion [2]
- **gd1989-12-09.fob.french.35373.sbeok.flac24**: source: Sennheiser MKE2002 omni's HRTF (baffled omni's) -> Sony TC-D5M, FOB/DFC in the center of a giant quiet zone of tapers and friends. Mics at 6'5". I was also… [3]. Also: Mike French made the transfers and master disc burn; Bob Loy added ID3 tags [3]
- **gd1989-12-09.sbd.miller-ladner.5450.shnf**: taped by DAT > CDR transfer - via C. Miller; transferred by DAE, tracking (EAC > cdwave > shntool > mkwact) and FTP/ABGD via C. Ladner; source: SBD > DAT > CDR > WAV > SHNv3 [6]

## Art and photos

- Poster by @donelichterman: [Don’s Pick on The Grateful Dead Live from the Great Western Forum on December 9, 1989 - The Grateful Dead Live](https://thegratefuldeadlive.com/the-grateful-dead-at-great-western-forum/) [26]
